subject: Management link jitter during rolling API upgrade — mitigation plan & evidence request
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@medisys.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Management plane errors after today's API rolling upgrade

Hi Kimberly,

We pushed the scheduled API management plane upgrade at 14:00 PDT to our Private deployment. Since then we've seen a spike in transient control-channel errors between our edge proxies and Redwood's management endpoint: roughly 5–7% request failures and occasional control link resets for a subset of pods. Latency is elevated on the control link (p99 ~700ms) and a handful of jobs reported "handshake timeout" in the logs.

Can you confirm if there were any changes on Redwood's side coincident with the 14:00 rollout? We need an urgent call if you have one. We're attaching a small log bundle for you to review.

Attachment: medisys_local_logs_0530.tgz (referenced)

Thanks,
Julia Park
Director, Cloud Ops — Medisys Health
julia.park@medisys.com
+1 646-555-0199

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@medisys.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Management plane errors after today's API rolling upgrade

Hi Julia — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the logs. We saw elevated retry counts in our telemetry that line up with your timeframe. No intentional config change was scheduled on Redwood's management controlplane for that region at 14:00 — there was a regional autoscaler job that completed at 13:50 but it should not have affected controlchannel TLS handshakes.

Immediate actions:
- I'll get our infra team on a bridge now. Can you open a short Webex/Zoom and grant screen share for the controlplane logs?
- Please send the full medisy_local_bundle.tgz you referenced (we only have a trimmed set). Also, if you can provide the agent debug level on one affected node (systemd journal snippet), that will speed triage.

Workaround while we investigate: if you can temporarily increase the control-channel keepalive to 45s on your side (we saw smaller keepalive windows from some agents) that may reduce handshake churn. If you prefer, we can push an inbound rule to accept the older TLS renegotiation for a short window — but we'd rather avoid changing handshake policies without understanding root cause.

I'll loop in Aditya and Marcus for a deep-dive.

—Kim

Priority: P1 customer-impacting controlplane instability on Private deployment.
Ask:
- Aditya: can you capture recent managementlink traces for region-us-west-2 (INFRA-3421) and check server-side renegotiation counters?
- Marcus: please prepare a minimal evidence pack (runtime traces, kernel timing events, TLS renegotiate frames) and a safe keepalive patch we can propose to the customer.

Notes: avoid mass rollback. This looks like increased handshake churn on a subset of agents. If we need to change TLS acceptance windows, we should do it only after trace evidence.

Thanks — Kim

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 16:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Management plane errors after today's API rolling upgrade

Kim / Marcus — quick triage update: we've pulled server-side traces for the controllink pool that serves Medisys (us-west-2). Findings so far:
- A spike in TLS handshake renegotiation attempts between 14:02–14:18 local time correlated with a short-lived GC spike on the controlplane JVM (we're investigating a GC policy interaction with our connection manager).
- Several agent-side peers exhibited aggressive keepalive timers (<=10s) which amplified connection churn during the GC pause window.

Actions taken:
1) Increased connection acceptance window on the controlplane process for the impacted pool and throttled renegotiation backoff at 15:50 to reduce flapping (non-invasive, reversible).
2) Collected a full evidence bundle: managementlink-trace-0530.json.gz and medisy_control_link_logs_0530.tgz (attached).
3) Drafted a small client-side config patch to relax keepalive sampling for their affected agent versions — file: keepalive-config-patch.diff.

Short-term recommendation to Medisys: apply the keepalive patch to the small cohort of nodes that hit the low-timer behaviour, or we can apply a temporary acceptance window server-side while they roll the patch. I'll be on the call if they want our engineers to push the server-side band-aid.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Attachment: managementlink-trace-0530.json.gz (evidence), keepalive-config-patch.diff

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@medisys.com>, Alan Zheng <a.zheng@medisys.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: control link jitter during your 2026-05-30 rollout

Hi Julia / Alan — thanks again for your patience while we investigated. Below is a concise summary of what we found, what we did, and next steps.

Summary of impact:
- Time window: 2026-05-30 14:00–14:20 PDT.
- Symptom: intermittent management/control channel handshakes and elevated request error rate (~5–7% transient).

Root cause (short): a short GC pause on a controlplane JVM instance overlapped with a subset of Medisys agents using aggressive keepalive timers (<=10s). The overlap caused transient handshake renegotiation that led to connection churn and higher latencies.

What we did:
- Collected full traces and logs (attached).
- Temporarily widened the controlplane acceptance window at 15:50 to stabilize connections while the customer rolled the keepalive patch to affected agents.
- Provided a small config patch for their agent (keepalive-config-patch.diff) and recommended a staggered rollout.

Files shared (attachments): medisys_control_link_logs_0530.tgz, managementlink-trace-0530.json.gz, keepalive-config-patch.diff
Drive evidence: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-evidence-link
Redwood ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3421

Recommended follow-up actions:
- Medisys: complete the staggered agent config rollout and confirm stability for 48 hours.
- Redwood Infra: schedule a JVM GC policy review for controlplane processes serving Private customers (owner: Aditya Rao).
- Joint postmortem call next week to review timeline and controls (we propose Tue 2026-06-08 09:00 PDT).

If you can confirm that your fleet has stabilized, we'll open a formal postmortem doc and share a curated evidence pack and remediation timeline.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
